text:
Ashley: quick heads-up — after enabling session_stickiness we see KV cache global miss rate jump from 7% -> 26% on the chat prod cluster. spikes after ~2m of continuous user typing. anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
Matt: hmm. are we sure the cache key is stable across requests? last time a small normalization change exploded cardinality. can you paste the key-gen snippet?
Ashley: here is the key helper we use in runtime v3.2:
```
def make_kv_key(tenant, session_id, prefix):
    # session_id is full UUID from client
    return f"{tenant}:{session_id}:{prefix}"
```
Matt: ok that's the problem — session_id is full UUID and client sometimes rotates a subtoken per connection. we used to slice it to 8 chars for stickiness. full UUID + varying prefix length => fragmentation.
Li: profiling backs that up. sampled hotspot shows 48% of keys differ only in the session_id low bits. Most hits are for the same logical conversation but different physical session ids. also saw a lot of short-lived keys in the LRU tail.
Sanjay: can we add a normalizer that derives a session_fingerprint = hash(session_id)[:8] and use that instead? would preserve isolation but reduce cardinality. also consider trimming trailing whitespace in prefix before hashing — we saw different tokenization adding a space leading to new keys.
Ashley: good call. also noticed this in the logs:
```
kv_get miss tenant=acme session=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000 prefix="Hello\n" computed_key="acme:123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000:Hello\n"
kv_put tenant=acme session=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000 prefix="Hello" computed_key="acme:123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000:Hello"
```
Ashley: note the prefix has a trailing newline sometimes from the tokenizer, so we get two different keys for the same semantic prefix.
Dana: small changes we can try: 1) normalize prefix (strip/normalize whitespace + lower()) 2) derive short session fingerprint 3) run short TTL/bucketed-ttl for ephemeral prefixes to avoid long-term fragmentation. we can A/B these on a 5% subset. :white_check_mark:
Matt: also check eviction behavior — if many tiny keys push out larger long-lived entries, that could explain the latency bump too. maybe we should evict by logical conversation recency rather than raw insertion time.
Sanjay: experiment proposal: implement make_kv_key(tenant, fingerprint, norm_prefix) in a feature-flagged build, extend TTL for hits to 30m on hot prefixes, and run k6 load with scripted token streaming to mimic continuous typing. compare miss rate and memory RSS after 30m.
Ashley: i'll roll an experiment tomorrow. posting perf baseline here so we can compare: miss_rate=0.26, median_latency_tokens=38ms, rss_per_shard=5.2GB.
Li: ping me once you have traces — i'll add flamegraphs for kv_get/kv_put and run key-cardinality histogram.
Ashley: thanks all. will update results in this thread. :thumbsup:
